items.labelEn: Life of a single thunderstorm cell
items.conditions: One thunderstorm cell, from developing to dissipating stage. Multicell clusters and supercells last longer. The value is the midpoint of the 30-60 min range given by the source, not a stated typical value.
items.conditionsFr: Une seule cellule orageuse, du stade de développement à la dissipation. Les orages multicellulaires et les supercellules durent plus longtemps. La valeur est le milieu de la plage de 30 à 60 min donnée par la source, pas une valeur typique publiée.
items.quote: The life time a single thunderstorm cell ranges from 30 to 60 minutes.
items.confidenceNotes: NWS spotter training material; only the range is sourced. Midpoint flagged as such. | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: value = middle of the published range; shown as illustrative with that range.

items.labelEn: Time between two eruptions of Old Faithful
items.labelFr: Intervalle entre deux éruptions du geyser Old Faithful
items.conditions: Old Faithful Geyser, Yellowstone. Median interval as of January 2025 (± 10 min prediction window); observed intervals range from 54 to 118 min. The interval drifts over the years.
items.conditionsFr: Geyser Old Faithful, Yellowstone. Intervalle médian en janvier 2025 (prévision à ± 10 min près) ; les intervalles observés vont de 54 à 118 min. L'intervalle évolue au fil des années.
items.locator: Old Faithful Area Frequently Asked Questions, 'How often does Old Faithful Geyser erupt?'
items.quote: as of January 2025, it is 102 minutes ± 10 minutes, with intervals ranging from 54 to 118 minutes.
items.confidenceNotes: Official NPS figure, dated by the source. Value is a median from park monitoring.

items.labelEn: Length of an Old Faithful eruption
items.conditions: Old Faithful Geyser, Yellowstone; normal eruptions. The value is the midpoint of the 1.5-5 min range given by the source, not a stated typical value.
items.conditionsFr: Geyser Old Faithful, Yellowstone ; éruptions normales. La valeur est le milieu de la plage de 1,5 à 5 min donnée par la source, pas une valeur typique publiée.
items.locator: Old Faithful Area Frequently Asked Questions, 'How long does it last?'
items.quote: Eruptions normally last between 1½ to 5 minutes
items.confidenceNotes: Range is sourced; midpoint flagged. Could be shown as a range only. | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: value = middle of the published range; shown as illustrative with that range.

items.labelFr: Cyclone tropical le plus long jamais observé (Freddy, 2023)
items.conditions: Tropical Cyclone Freddy, South Indian Ocean, February-March 2023: world record for the longest-running tropical cyclone in NOAA AOML's table of records. A typical hurricane lasts far less (days to about a week).
items.conditionsFr: Cyclone tropical Freddy, océan Indien Sud, février-mars 2023 : record mondial de durée dans le tableau des records de la NOAA (AOML). Un ouragan ordinaire dure bien moins (quelques jours à environ une semaine).
items.locator: Hurricane FAQ, table of tropical cyclone records, row 'Longest running'
items.quote: Longest running 2023 Tropical Cyclone Freddy South Indian Ocean 36 days
items.confidenceNotes: Record value, not typical. Older pages (e.g. hurricanescience.org) still give Hurricane/Typhoon John, 1994, 31 days: superseded. The 'days to about a week' remark in conditions is context only, not a sourced value.

items.labelEn: Age of Methuselah, the oldest known living tree
items.labelFr: Âge de Mathusalem, le plus vieil arbre vivant connu
items.conditions: Great Basin bristlecone pine 'Methuselah', White Mountains, California; age from tree-ring count of a core taken in 1957, as stated by NPS (the page does not say for which year the age is given).
items.conditionsFr: Pin Bristlecone du Grand Bassin « Mathusalem », White Mountains, Californie ; âge obtenu par comptage des cernes d'une carotte prélevée en 1957, tel qu'indiqué par le NPS (la page ne précise pas l'année de référence).
items.locator: Great Basin Bristlecone Pine page, paragraph on the oldest living tree
items.quote: The oldest LIVING tree is called "Methuselah" and is 4,765 years old.
items.confidenceNotes: Uncertain reference year: the 1957 core date is not stated on this page (it comes from other sources). Other sources give 4,789 (USDA, page returned 403, not opened) to about 4,850 years (age updated to the current year). Order of magnitude solid; last digits not.

items.conditions: Giant sequoia in the Converse Basin Grove (Giant Sequoia National Monument), age from ring count; oldest known specimen of the species.
items.conditionsFr: Séquoia géant du bosquet de Converse Basin (Giant Sequoia National Monument), âge obtenu par comptage des cernes ; plus vieux spécimen connu de l'espèce.
items.locator: Sequoia Research, 'How long do tree species live?'
items.quote: the oldest known specimen to have been 3,266 years old in the Converse Basin Grove of Giant Sequoia National Monument
items.confidenceNotes: NPS figure; the specimen was a felled tree (past tense 'to have been'). Another NPS page (Sequoia & Kings Canyon) says 'up to 3,400 years' without detail.

items.labelEn: Ruby-throated hummingbird's non-stop flight across the Gulf of Mexico
items.labelFr: Traversée sans escale du golfe du Mexique par le colibri à gorge rubis
items.conditions: Migratory flight of about 500 miles (800 km) over the Gulf of Mexico. The value is the midpoint of the 18-20 h range given by the source.
items.conditionsFr: Vol migratoire d'environ 800 km (500 miles) au-dessus du golfe du Mexique. La valeur est le milieu de la plage de 18 à 20 h donnée par la source.
items.locator: NETN Species Spotlight, section 'What is it?'
items.quote: a 500-mile, 18-20 hour migratory flight across the Gulf of Mexico
items.confidenceNotes: NPS popular-science article without a cited study; plausible but secondary in nature. Midpoint flagged. | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: value = middle of the published range; shown as illustrative with that range.

items.labelEn: Time between two heartbeats of a ruby-throated hummingbird
items.labelFr: Intervalle entre deux battements de cœur du colibri à gorge rubis
items.conditions: Heart rate of 1,200 beats per minute stated by the source (activity level not specified); interval = 60 s / 1,200.
items.conditionsFr: Fréquence cardiaque de 1 200 battements par minute indiquée par la source (niveau d'activité non précisé) ; intervalle = 60 s / 1 200.
items.locator: NETN Species Spotlight, paragraph on flight adaptations
items.quote: a large heart (beating 1200 times per minute)
items.confidenceNotes: Single popular-science figure without activity state; other non-federal sources give about 600 bpm at rest up to more than 1,000 bpm in flight. Treat as order of magnitude (tens of milliseconds).

items.conditions: Eastern North American monarchs, fall migration to the overwintering forests in Mexico, at 50-100 miles (80-160 km) a day. The source gives an upper bound ('up to two months'), converted here as 2 × 30 days.
items.conditionsFr: Monarques de l'est de l'Amérique du Nord, migration d'automne vers les forêts d'hivernage du Mexique, à raison de 80 à 160 km par jour. La source donne une borne haute (« jusqu'à deux mois »), convertie ici en 2 × 30 jours.
items.locator: Monarch Butterfly Migration and Overwintering, paragraph after the Biosphere Reserve
items.quote: Monarchs can travel between 50-100 miles a day; it can take up to two months to complete their journey.
items.confidenceNotes: Upper bound, not a typical duration; the 30-day month conversion is ours. Other organisations (not opened) describe a mid-August to mid-November season, which is the migration window, not one butterfly's trip.

items.labelEn: One orbit of the International Space Station
items.labelFr: Un tour de la Terre par la Station spatiale internationale
items.conditions: ISS in low Earth orbit at about five miles (8 km) per second; NASA states 'about every 90 minutes', i.e. 16 orbits in 24 hours.
items.conditionsFr: ISS en orbite basse, à environ 8 km par seconde ; la NASA indique « environ toutes les 90 minutes », soit 16 orbites en 24 heures.
items.locator: Space Station Facts and Figures, introduction
items.confidenceNotes: Rounded official figure ('about'); actual period varies slightly with altitude (about 92-93 min at current altitudes, not sourced here).

items.labelEn: Apollo 11: from launch to entering lunar orbit
items.labelFr: Apollo 11 : du décollage à la mise en orbite lunaire
items.conditions: Apollo 11, July 1969: time from launch (16 July) to the first lunar orbit insertion burn (19 July), about 75 h 50 min (75.83 h); includes the time spent in Earth parking orbit.
items.conditionsFr: Apollo 11, juillet 1969 : temps écoulé entre le décollage (16 juillet) et la première manœuvre d'insertion en orbite lunaire (19 juillet), environ 75 h 50 min (75,83 h) ; inclut le temps passé en orbite d'attente terrestre.
items.quote: At about 75 hours, 50 minutes into the flight, a retrograde firing of the SPS for 357.5 seconds
items.confidenceNotes: Mission elapsed time from NASA; conversion 75 h 50 min = 75.83 h is ours.

items.labelEn: Concorde Paris–New York scheduled flight time
items.labelFr: Temps de vol prévu du Concorde Paris–New York
items.conditions: Air France Concorde, schedule announced for the October 2001 relaunch: Paris–New York 3 h 55 min (previously 3 h 45 min, lengthened for air traffic restrictions); New York–Paris 3 h 45 min. Value = 3 h 55 min.
items.conditionsFr: Concorde d'Air France, horaire annoncé pour la reprise des vols en octobre 2001 : Paris–New York 3 h 55 (au lieu de 3 h 45, allongé pour tenir compte des restrictions de trafic aérien) ; New York–Paris 3 h 45. Valeur = 3 h 55.
items.locator: Section I 'On board the Air France Concorde', opening paragraph
items.quote: The recently announced flight time from Paris to New York is 3hr 55min instead of 3hr 45min to take into account air traffic restrictions
items.confidenceNotes: Primary operator text, but read on a secondary host (Air France and British Airways heritage pages could not be opened). The often-quoted '3 h 30' is airborne time, not this scheduled time. Record (2 h 52 min 59 s, BA, 1996) not verified here.

items.labelEn: Fastest scheduled TGV from Paris to Lyon
items.labelFr: TGV le plus rapide de Paris à Lyon (horaire)
items.conditions: TGV INOUI trains Paris Gare de Lyon → Lyon Part-Dieu listed in SNCF open data for 4 December 2026 (20 trains): fastest 1 h 56 min, slowest 2 h 10 min. OUIGO trains and other Lyon stations are not in this dataset.
items.conditionsFr: TGV INOUI Paris Gare de Lyon → Lyon Part-Dieu listés dans les données ouvertes SNCF pour le 4 décembre 2026 (20 trains) : le plus rapide 1 h 56, le plus lent 2 h 10. Les OUIGO et les autres gares de Lyon ne figurent pas dans ce jeu de données.
items.locator: Explore API v2.1, dataset tgvmax, records date=2026-12-04, FRPLY→FRLPD (e.g. train 6643)
items.confidenceNotes: Official SNCF timetable data, but one day only and only trains listed for TGVmax booking (may omit some trains). The minimum 1 h 56 recurs on 11 of the 20 trains. Snapshot will change with timetables. | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: timetable durations read in the open-data records (fastest 116 min, slowest 130 min); the derivation is a subtraction of scheduled times: duration = heure_arrivee - heure_depart for each record; value = min (116 min), low = min, high = max (130 min)

items.labelEn: Time between two trains on Paris Métro line 14 at rush hour
items.labelFr: Intervalle entre deux métros de la ligne 14 à l'heure de pointe
items.conditions: Paris Métro line 14 (automatic, driverless), peak hours, since April 2025.
items.conditionsFr: Ligne 14 du métro parisien (automatique, sans conducteur), heures de pointe, depuis avril 2025.
items.locator: Press release of 29 January 2026, page 1, section 'Fréquentation record pour la ligne 14'
items.quote: intervalle de 85 secondes en heure de pointe entre deux trains depuis avril 2025.
items.confidenceNotes: Operator's planned headway, not a measured average.

items.labelEn: Turnaround of a Boeing 737-800 at the gate
items.conditions: Manufacturer planning chart: 737-800 with 162 passengers in 2 classes, one door, 100 % passenger and cargo exchange, full servicing including refuelling; ideal conditions for a single airplane. Airlines often plan differently.
items.conditionsFr: Diagramme de planification du constructeur : 737-800 avec 162 passagers en 2 classes, une porte, échange complet des passagers et du fret, service complet avec avitaillement ; conditions idéales pour un seul avion. Les compagnies planifient souvent autrement.
items.locator: Section 5.2.4 'Terminal Operations – Turnaround Station: Model 737-800, -800W', page 5-11, chart title
items.confidenceNotes: Read from the chart graphic (not extractable text) at 300 dpi; manufacturer's idealised schedule, not an airline average. Section 5.0 states the data 'reflect ideal conditions for a single airplane'.
